newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close mostly lower with cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close mostly lower with cash.

text.p: Further weakness in cash lumber kept most months of CME lumber futures pressured into the close with rolling out of spot May adding to declines in that month, traders said.
Lumber ended $6.80 per thousand board feet lower to $0.90 higher with only November up. May paced the gain at $382.70 and July finished down $2.40 at $384.50 per tbf.

Cash spruce continued to decline and expectations that cash prices will ease further pressured futures. Secondaries continued to discount mill prices and mills were offering wood at prices under the current offical quote, traders said.
"I know of people that have bought spruce around $378 and futures are telling us (cash) should be down around $370," a cash source said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $388 per tbf, off $9 from both Friday and last week-ago levels. But they also said some western spruce producers were looking for business in the mid $380 and one mill accepted $380.
Cash prices may have to go down into the $365 to $370 area, where mills have found increased interest for wood peviously, before the market can find support, traders added.
